title: Quentin and the Alibi
premise: Yara Thackeray, the reclusive archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, receives two letters from a stranger claiming to be their half-sibling: one confessing to a murder in the cathedral's sealed crypt decades ago, one promising Yara a share of an inheritance if they can decode a ledger hidden among the cathedral's own records. As Yara follows the ledger's cipher through baptismal registers and mortuary rolls, they uncover that the 'murder' was their mother's staged death, orchestrated by the Thackeray family to erase a scandal, and that the crypt holds proof. The twin letters were sent by two rival claimants—one protecting the secret, one weaponizing it—and Yara must choose between exposing the family that abandoned them or destroying the evidence to protect the only person who ever chose them. In the end, Yara opens the crypt publicly, claims their name, and lets the inheritance go.
about_author: Elodie Crane is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing centuries of births, marriages, and burials before turning to fiction. They write quiet mysteries about people who live in the margins of official histories.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet Yara cataloguing the cathedral archive, invisible by choice, tending documents no one reads. A routine request from the dean forces them into contact with living people for the first time in months. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, cracked open by small human friction.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Two letters arrive on the same morning: one confessing to a killing in the locked crypt in 1974, one promising Yara a fortune if they find 'what was written twice.' The handwriting is identical. Emotional beat: dread braided with a terrible thrill—someone knows Yara exists.

chapters.title: What the Register Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Searching the 1974 burial records, Yara finds their own surname—Thackeray—on a crypt interment they never knew existed: a woman listed as Yara's mother, buried alive in paperwork though her body is elsewhere. Emotional beat: vertigo; the archive turns mirror.

chapters.title: The Dean's Polite Warning
chapters.summary: Dean Ambrose's POV. The dean, charming and watchful, warns Yara off 'historical curiosities' and reveals he too received a letter years ago and burned it. Emotional beat: the first hint that the cathedral itself is complicit, and kindness can be a leash.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Mortuary Rolls
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following the letter's clue, Yara discovers the ledger hidden as marginalia across decades of mortuary rolls—a double-entry record where every legitimate burial has a shadow entry. Emotional beat: exhilaration of pattern, quickly soured by what the shadows record.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Lychgate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A man named Corwin Thackeray appears, claiming to be Yara's half-brother, warm and plausible, pressing for the ledger. Emotional beat: hunger for family warring with instinct; Yara lies for the first time in years and finds it easy, which frightens them.

chapters.title: The Second Claimant
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A woman, Maren, arrives claiming she sent both letters—that the confession was bait to draw Yara out, because the crypt holds proof that could free her father, imprisoned for the 1974 death. Emotional beat: betrayal, then recalibration; the confession was theater.

chapters.title: Ledger of Shadows
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with flashbacks. Decoding deeper, Yara reconstructs the scheme: the Thackerays used the crypt as a private vault, staging deaths to move money and people—including Yara's mother, who didn't die in 1974 but vanished into it. Emotional beat: grief reframed; Yara was erased, not orphaned.

chapters.title: Corwin's Version
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Corwin genuinely believes his father killed a blackmailer in the crypt and that the ledger will clear the family name. He courts Yara sincerely, which makes his manipulation worse. Emotional beat: sympathy for the devil; duty dressed as love.

chapters.title: Maren's Version
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confesses her real stake: her father took the fall for a Thackeray, and the crypt's true contents would exonerate him. She offers Yara partnership—and something more dangerous, being seen. Emotional beat: love against duty begins its argument.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Using archival keys and a night when the dean is away, Yara reaches the crypt door and finds it already opened from inside—recently. Someone is ahead of them. Emotional beat: violation of the one place that was supposed to be still.

chapters.title: What Was Written Twice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Inside, Yara finds the crypt's inner chamber stripped except for one thing left deliberately: a second ledger, the original, with Yara's mother's handwriting in the margins—she was the archivist before Yara, and she hid the truth in plain sight for her child to find. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness across decades.

chapters.title: Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, interleaved with the mother's marginal notes. The annotations reveal the mother survived, lived under a new name, and died three years ago—leaving everything to whoever decoded her ledger. Emotional beat: mourning someone who was alive all along; anger and love in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Dean's Debt
chapters.summary: Dean Ambrose's POV. Confronted, the dean admits the church helped bury the scandal in exchange for endowments, and begs Yara to let it stay buried—for the cathedral's soul, he claims, meaning its finances. Emotional beat: institutional rot wearing vestments; Yara refuses.

chapters.title: Corwin's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Cornered by family lawyers, Corwin gives Yara twenty-four hours to hand over the original ledger or face a forged accusation of theft—the same trick used on Maren's father. Emotional beat: the mask drops; duty revealed as coercion.

chapters.title: Alibi in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Realizing the title's meaning—the ledger itself is the alibi, timestamped proof the 1974 death was staged—Yara works through the night with Maren to authenticate it against the archive's own paper stock. Emotional beat: two outsiders building trust in the dark; love choosing itself over safety.

chapters.title: Twenty-Four Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating Yara/Corwin/Maren POVs. The deadline compresses: Corwin's lawyers move, the dean wavers toward self-preservation, and Maren urges burning the ledger to protect her father from reopened wounds. Emotional beat: every alliance strained; Yara alone must decide what the truth is for.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. Corwin comes for the ledger; in the crypt confrontation, Yara reveals the final entry—the staged death was ordered by Corwin's own beloved grandmother, not his father. His duty collapses. Emotional beat: truth as a blade that cuts the wielder too.

chapters.title: Opening the Doors
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Instead of selling or burning the ledger, Yara places it in the cathedral's public exhibition, names their mother in the records, and files the exoneration for Maren's father. Emotional beat: invisibility renounced; belonging claimed on Yara's own terms.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Thackeray money evaporates in legal fallout; what remains is the mother's modest bequest and her marginalia. Yara declines Corwin's last, genuine apology but keeps one letter. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not wealth, but witness.

chapters.title: The New Archivist's Hand
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Months later, Maren visits; her father is free; she and Yara begin something unhurried. Yara trains a successor, teaching the marginalia habit forward. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the archive becomes a home rather than a hiding place.

chapters.title: What Remains Written
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, closing frame. Yara adds their own entry to the ledger—an honest account of everything—and locks the crypt not to hide it, but because some doors should be opened deliberately. Emotional beat: peace earned; the story ends with a hand writing, not a door closing.
